Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. _Reviewed July 25, 2026, 6:00 AM ET / 10:00 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes This PR activates catalog lifecycle status in model selection so default and configured pickers hide deprecated or disabled provider rows while curated provider manifests remove older model entries. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked until real behavior proof is added - 7 items remain** Keep this PR open for maintainer handling. The picker filter is applied after every catalog view is constructed, so it also hides deprecated and disabled rows from the documented `provider-config` inventory view rather than limiting curation to default/configured picker views; the PR also needs real after-fix behavior proof before merge. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `8c6aa912432f0aafe2903b020150c8ca0e3924d6` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | The PR has focused tests described in its body, but the unconditional inventory filter is a blocking correctness defect and no real after-fix behavior proof is attached. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Needs real behavior proof before merge: The PR body reports focused automated suites, but it does not include inspectable after-fix CLI, Gateway, or Control UI evidence showing the curated picker and preserved legacy-reference behavior; please redact private model/account details before attaching proof. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Needs proof | Needs real behavior proof before merge: The PR body reports focused automated suites, but it does not include inspectable after-fix CLI, Gateway, or Control UI evidence showing the curated picker and preserved legacy-reference behavior; please redact private model/account details before attaching proof. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 4 items | Unconditional visibility filter: The PR projects the complete result and then filters it with `isPickerVisibleCatalogEntry` without checking the requested view, so lifecycle-hidden rows are removed from every view handled by this function.
Documented provider inventory contract: The PR documentation says `view: "provider-config"` is the provider inventory view and should show source-authored rows without picker filtering, while the new final filter applies there as well.
Focused test gap: The new visibility tests cover `default`, `configured`, and `all`, but do not cover `provider-config`, which is the view affected by the unconditional final filter. | | **Findings** | 1 actionable finding | [P1] Limit lifecycle filtering to picker views | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Provider plugins contribute static model catalogs, which OpenClaw loads and projects into logical model routes before the Gateway serves CLI, Control UI, and chat-picker views. The changed visibility policy sits after route projection and determines which catalog entries each Gateway model view returns. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Provider manifests] --> B[Catalog loader] B --> C[Logical route projection] C --> D[Visibility policy] D --> E[Gateway model views] E --> F[CLI, Control UI, and chat pickers] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should the approved curation policy hide lifecycle-deprecated rows only from default/configured pickers while keeping the `provider-config` inventory complete? | **Keep inventory views complete:** Restrict lifecycle hiding to default and configured picker views and retain every provider-authored row in `all` and `provider-config` views. | Why: The PR states a maintainer-directed product decision, but the current implementation conflicts with the documented inventory-view boundary; maintainers need to confirm the intended permanent view contract. ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Needs real behavior proof before merge: The PR body reports focused automated suites, but it does not include inspectable after-fix CLI, Gateway, or Control UI evidence showing the curated picker and preserved legacy-reference behavior; please redact private model/account details before attaching proof. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Limit lifecycle filtering to picker views (P1)** - The final filter runs for every view, including `provider-config`. That view is documented as the unfiltered provider inventory, so deprecated and disabled rows now disappear from it. Apply lifecycle hiding only to the default/configured picker views and add a `provider-config` regression test. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The intentional curation changes default discovery across several providers; maintainers should explicitly confirm the current-generation policy and preserve the documented full-inventory escape hatches before merge. - [ ] **Improve patch quality** - Restrict lifecycle filtering to `default` and `configured` views and cover `provider-config` in the focused visibility suite. - [ ] **Improve patch quality** - Attach redacted live CLI, Gateway, or Control UI output showing deprecated rows hidden in a picker and visible in the full inventory. - [ ] **Improve patch quality** - After updating the PR body with proof, request a maintainer `@clawsweeper re-review` if a new review is not triggered automatically. ## Findings - [P1] Limit lifecycle filtering to picker views — `src/agents/model-catalog-visibility.ts:346-348`

Migration or upgrade compatibility proof is recorded; maintainers should verify it before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Scope filtering to picker views (recommended)** Guard the lifecycle filter so `default` and `configured` are curated while `all` and `provider-config` retain the full catalog, with focused regression tests. 2. **Accept a broader inventory change** Keep the unconditional filter only if maintainers intentionally redefine `provider-config` as a curated view and approve the resulting compatibility change. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Limit lifecycle hiding to the default and configured picker views, preserve `all` and `provider-config` inventories, add regression coverage for each view, and attach redacted live evidence showing both the curated picker and a retained legacy configured reference. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: call `models.list` through the `provider-config` view with a catalog row marked `deprecated` or `disabled`; the final unconditional filter removes that row despite the documented complete-inventory contract. Is this the best way to solve the issue? No. Activating lifecycle metadata at the shared seam is a maintainable approach, but applying it after all views are assembled also changes the non-picker `provider-config` inventory; the filter should be restricted to the curated picker views. Full review comments: - [P1] Limit lifecycle filtering to picker views — `src/agents/model-catalog-visibility.ts:346-348` The final filter runs for every view, including `provider-config`. That view is documented as the unfiltered provider inventory, so deprecated and disabled rows now disappear from it. Apply lifecycle hiding only to the default/configured picker views and add a `provider-config` regression test. Confidence: 0.96 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.96 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Maintainer decision on the rank-up question — **yes, lifecycle hiding is restricted to the default/configured picker views; inventory views stay complete.** That is the implemented behavior, not a follow-up:

- `view: "all"` early-returns before the picker filter in `resolveLogicalVisibleModelCatalog` (`src/agents/model-catalog-visibility.ts` — `projectEntries(params.catalog)` return path precedes `isPickerVisibleCatalogEntry`).
- `view: "provider-config"` never enters that function at all (`buildModelsListResult` early return in `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-result.ts`).
- Covered by tests: `model-catalog-visibility.test.ts` ("keeps deprecated and disabled rows in the all inventory") and `src/gateway/server-methods/models.test.ts` (provider-config unfiltered).

Real Gateway behavior proof (dev gateway, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` set, this branch at head `8c6aa912432f`), via `openclaw gateway call models.list`:

`{"view":"configured"}` (the picker view) — openai rows:

```text
gpt-5.6
gpt-5.6-luna
gpt-5.6-sol
gpt-5.6-terra
```

`{"view":"all"}` — full curated inventory, hidden rows retained and ancient rows gone:

```text
openai:   gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.6, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra
anthropic: claude-fable-5, claude-haiku-4-5, claude-mythos-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5
zai:      glm-5.1, glm-5.2
moonshot: kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed, kimi-k3
deepseek: deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-pro
```

Pinned-model guarantee — with `agents.defaults.model.primary: "openai/gpt-5.5"`, the configured picker view becomes:

```text
gpt-5.5
gpt-5.6
gpt-5.6-luna
gpt-5.6-sol
gpt-5.6-terra
```

The deprecated pin stays visible, exactly as documented in `docs/concepts/models.md`. Uncataloged refs (e.g. a deleted `openai/o3` primary plus `openai/o1` session override with empty `modelPolicy.allow`) remain selectable, proven in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts`. CLI `openclaw models list --provider openai` intentionally keeps inventory semantics (it is the documented place to find exact refs for allowlists).

Merged via squash.
